extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: An elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans to evaluate large vision-language models (LVLMs) across 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, ensuring visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and advanced multi-modal capabilities.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.publisher: University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory
extraction.citeAs: Chen et al., "Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models?", arXiv:2403.20330v2, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from current benchmarks (SEED, AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU) with an automated pipeline using eight powerful LLMs as inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage. Then, 16 leading LVLMs were used to gauge difficulty, and strict manual review by three experts was applied to curate 1,500 high-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples were sourced from existing multi-modal benchmarks: SEED, AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated pipeline filtered out samples that could be answered by more than 2 of 8 LLMs (to exclude leaking or visual-unnecessary problems). Then, 16 LVLMs were used to split samples into four difficulty levels. Finally, manual review ensured visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and coverage of capability dimensions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations (labels) were derived from the original benchmarks; no new annotations were created. The paper does not describe a separate annotation protocol for the curated dataset.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, etc.) were used as inspectors; 16 LVLMs (GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series, etc.) were used for difficulty gauging.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies that existing benchmarks have samples where visual content is unnecessary and unintentional data leakage occurs, leading to misjudgment of LVLM capabilities. MMStar aims to mitigate these biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited to 1,500 samples and may not cover all possible multi-modal capabilities. The paper notes that even the best model scores under 60% on average, indicating room for improvement.
